text: Everything so far has been building toward this file. The source is declared, the staging model is clean, the tests prove it's trustworthy. Now we build the mart — the final, reportable table Jaffle Shop's Ops Manager would actually query.

Here's the real file: models, marts, customers dot sql. A customers CTE selecting from ref, stg_jaffle_shop__customers — not source(), ref(). Then a final select of customer_id, first_name, last_name. That's this project's actual deliverable: the answer to Lesson one's ask.

Notice that function call: ref, not source. That's the real difference in practice. source() points at raw data this project didn't build — raw_customers. ref() points at a model this project already built — the staging model from Lesson six. Same idea as the dbt course taught, now applied for real.

You might notice this mart model looks almost identical to the staging model underneath it. That's not a shortcut — it's honest. This Beginner project only has one source table, so there's nothing yet to join, and no business logic yet to compute. The Intermediate capstone, next in this series, is where joining in order history actually changes that.

Build it with dbt run, select customers. Because customers dot sql references the staging model with ref(), dbt automatically knows to build that staging model first if it isn't already built — dependency-aware build order, straight from the project's own DAG.

With customers built, the chain from raw data to tested, reportable table is complete, start to finish. Next lesson, we run the whole project at once with dbt build and read a real, complete pass-fail output, line by line.
